limitation: Task/event retention was not found to retain UObject, embedded tick, prerequisites backing or world. Unique CAS dequeue applies to one enqueued queue node, not global duplicate insertion/manual redispatch. No explicit-destruction/GC/concurrent-writer retirement lease was established. No source/Ghidra changes occurred in this follow-up. Stored decompilation reflects existing annotations, which were verified only for the bounded facts reported.

/* Summary: Dispatches a component tick through native liveness, registration, tick-type and owner
   time-dilation guards.
   
   Parameters:
   pTickFunction: process-local tick-function binding with target component at +0x50.
   flDeltaSeconds: engine interval delta in XMM1.
   nLevelTick: engine level-tick selector in R8D.
   
   Algorithm:
   1. Build a 12-byte local call context: tick-function pointer followed by level-tick selector.
   2. Read target component +0x188 bit 11 as the special level-tick admission flag.
   3. Call 141D2CAC0 with component, flag, delta, selector and address of local context.
   4. Return only after the complete guarded component call.
   
   Returns:
   Void.
   
   Source:
   Native assembly 141D43230..141D43269. Vtable slot +8 at 143865FA0, diagnostic-message slot
   141D41E40 emits [TickComponent]. Vtable 143865F98 is installed by 14237F8F0 and 141D31450.
   
   Replay relevance:
   Helper 141D2CAC0 validates UObject flags 0x30000000, invokes component virtual +0x350, checks
   +0x188 bit 0, resolves owner at +0x190, applies special level-tick rules, and scales delta by
   owner +0x80 or 1.0. It invokes component virtual +0x300 with the original tick-function pointer
   in R9. This includes derived particle fade, completion and destruction work; skipping it is not
   presentation-neutral. Any resumable host continuation must retain logical arguments and validated
   bindings, never this function's stack context.
   
   Special Cases:
   Incoming R9 and stack arguments are not consumed by this concrete implementation. The 12-byte
   local context is valid only for the synchronous helper call. local_28 is the outgoing
   fifth-argument slot, not retained state. Secondary/custom tick-function implementations and
   asynchronous component tasks require separate ownership audit. */

void DispatchComponentTickFunction(void *pTickFunction,float flDeltaSeconds,int nLevelTick)

{
  void *pDispatchTickFunction;
  int nDispatchLevelTick;
  
  pDispatchTickFunction = pTickFunction;
  nDispatchLevelTick = nLevelTick;
  FUN_141d2cac0(*(longlong *)((longlong)pTickFunction + 0x50),
                (byte)(*(uint *)(*(longlong *)((longlong)pTickFunction + 0x50) + 0x188) >> 0xb) & 1,
                flDeltaSeconds,nLevelTick,&pDispatchTickFunction);
  return;
}

/* Register or unregister all tick functions for an already registered actor component.
   
   Algorithm:
   1. Require component+0x188 bit0 (registered).
   2. Compare requested registration with component+0x188 bit29 (0x20000000).
   3. If different, dispatch virtual+0x2D8 with RCX=component and DL=fRegister.
   4. Clear global registration context144392300, then publish bit29.
   Returns:
   void. An unchanged request or unregistered component performs no work.
   
   Parameters:
   pActorComponent: UActorComponent_Partial*; live component, non-null.
   fRegister: bool; true registers, false unregisters. Microsoft x64 ABI, not x86 thiscall.
   
   Scheduling ownership:
   Bit29 is the tick-functions registration flag, NOT render dirtiness. The end-frame queue uses
   bits30..31 separately. Never mask bit29 without ownership of the registration lifecycle.
   The base virtual141D58AC0 unregisters primary tick+110 only when its +0C mask0x40 is set.
   Registration calls141D5FB60, whose mask0x02 CanEverTick gate must pass before scheduling.
   Therefore the verified base virtual with mask0x42 clear permits a logical registration change
   without scheduler membership, allocations or gameplay callbacks. Subclass overrides require
   separate audit.
   DestroyActorComponent141D41970 and UActorComponent_UnregisterAndDetach141D66700 consume bit29
   before virtual teardown.
   
   Evidence:
   Constructor141D31450 installs base vtable143865FB0, whose2D8 slot is141D58AC0. Actual PE
   instructions and a private-memory shipped-wrapper fixture verify reversible changes with an
   unchanged primary tick prefix. This is not general live historical restoration proof.
   
   Special Cases:
   The decompiler may show a register spill local_res8; it is not persistent state. The indirect
   virtual prototype may omit its implicit RCX/DL arguments; assembly establishes both. */

void RegisterAllComponentTickFunctions(UActorComponent_Partial *pActorComponent,bool fRegister)

{
  if (((*(uint *)&pActorComponent->field_0x188 & 1) != 0) &&
     ((*(uint *)&pActorComponent->field_0x188 >> 0x1d & 1) != (uint)fRegister)) {
    (**(code **)((longlong)(pActorComponent->objectBase).pVirtualTable + 0x2d8))();
    g_pCurrentActorComponentRegistrationContext = (UActorComponent_Partial *)0x0;
    *(uint *)&pActorComponent->field_0x188 =
         *(uint *)&pActorComponent->field_0x188 ^
         ((uint)fRegister << 0x1d ^ *(uint *)&pActorComponent->field_0x188) & 0x20000000;
  }
  return;
}
